parent_scheme.name: field_under_butterfly_wings
parent_scheme.secondary_language: five three-storey pavilions standing apart, each under a V-shaped butterfly roof - valleys catching the rain in the middle of every roof
parent_scheme.formal_principle: Rain and daylight both want to be collected at the centre of each pavilion, so every roof folds inward as a butterfly: five valleys in a field, each pavilion's two wings lifting its eaves outward to the yard.

ops.why: Input: five pavilions in a yard. Limit: height 0.55 declares mid; spread 1.6 keeps yard between.
Input: each pavilion collects rain and light at its centre. Limit: pitch 0.8 keeps the valley inside the cap on pavilions this size.

scheme.name: butterfly_field_wide_lanes
scheme.secondary_language: five three-storey pavilions under butterfly roofs, spread wider so no two plans touch, tied by a low shared ground plate
scheme.formal_principle: The field of V roofs is kept and the lanes are made real: spread 1.8 opens every gap to a lane a person walks down, and a low tie plate under the five gives the field one ground and one address.
scheme.dominant_gesture: a field of V roofs on one tie plate
scheme.reference_basis: development of field_under_butterfly_wings: the field of V roofs is kept; the jury's overlap, frontage and core remarks are answered
scheme.design_argument_ko: 겹치던 평면을 벌려 골목을 만들고 낮은 공용 판이 다섯을 하나의 밭으로 묶는다.

ops.why: Spread 1.8 answers the overlapping plans: every pavilion stands clear; tie 0.3 gives the cluster one shared ground plate so the field reads as one project.
Every roof still folds inward as a butterfly - the valley is the idea and is kept in every child.

scheme.name: butterfly_field_with_a_canopy
scheme.secondary_language: five pavilions under butterfly roofs, a shared canopy reaching toward the open side as the field's front
scheme.formal_principle: A field needs a front: the pavilions keep their valleys, and one canopy reaches out toward the open side so the street reads an entry and the cluster gains the frontage hierarchy the jury missed.
scheme.dominant_gesture: a field of V roofs with a front canopy
scheme.reference_basis: development of field_under_butterfly_wings: the field of V roofs is kept; the jury's overlap, frontage and core remarks are answered
scheme.design_argument_ko: 열린 변으로 뻗는 캐노피가 밭에 정면과 입구를 준다.

ops.why: Five pavilions kept at the parent's scale; tie 0.2 adds a thin shared ground.
Every roof still folds inward as a butterfly - the valley is the idea and is kept in every child.
A canopy toward the open side gives the field a front and an entry the jury said it lacked.

scheme.name: butterfly_field_toward_the_street
scheme.secondary_language: five pavilions under butterfly roofs, the whole field pushed toward the open side so it fronts the street
scheme.formal_principle: A field needs a front: the pavilions keep their valleys and the cluster moves toward the open side, so the street meets the first pavilions instead of a leftover strip - the frontage hierarchy the jury missed.
scheme.reference_basis: development of field_under_butterfly_wings: the field of V roofs is kept; the jury's overlap, frontage and core remarks are answered
scheme.design_argument_ko: 밭 전체를 열린 변으로 밀어 거리가 첫 파빌리온과 만나게 한다.

ops.why: Five pavilions spread 1.7 so plans clear; a tie plate is the court floor.
Every roof still folds inward as a butterfly - the valley is the idea and is kept in every child.
The field grows toward the open side so its front reaches the street; the west tip stops being empty.

scheme.name: butterfly_field_of_four_lifted
scheme.secondary_language: four larger pavilions under butterfly roofs, lifted on supports so the whole ground is one public field
scheme.formal_principle: Fewer, larger houses and a free ground: four pavilions give each a floor plate that takes a core, and lifting them makes the ground under the field continuous - the public room the gaps only hinted at.
scheme.dominant_gesture: four lifted V-roof pavilions over one ground
scheme.reference_basis: development of field_under_butterfly_wings: the field of V roofs is kept; the jury's overlap, frontage and core remarks are answered
scheme.design_argument_ko: 네 채로 줄여 코어를 넣고, 들어 올려 지면 전체를 공용 밭으로 만든다.

ops.why: Four pavilions answer the core-per-house remark: each plate is large enough for its own core.
Lifting frees the ground as one continuous public field under the roofs.
Shallower valleys so the top floor is not cut by the pitch, as the jury noted; said after the lift so the raised houses carry them.
